blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Glen Waverley in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of adding space to your Glen Waverley home? We break down extension costs, pricing factors, and what to budget in 2026.
body: If you own a home in Glen Waverley, you've probably looked at your living room and wondered whether extending out or up is worth it. With property prices in Melbourne's east still climbing, a well-planned extension can add serious value — often more than the cost of the build itself. But the big question is always cost. In this guide, we'll give you a realistic look at what home extension prices look like in Glen Waverley in 2026, based on our experience building here for over a decade.

Let's start with a simple rule: expect to pay between $3,000 and $5,500 per square metre for a standard single-storey extension in Glen Waverley. That range covers everything from basic finishes to mid-range fittings. A typical three-bedroom extension of around 40 square metres will set you back anywhere from $120,000 to $220,000. Factors like site access, soil conditions, and the complexity of the connection to your existing structure all push the price one way or the other.

Double-storey extensions cost more per square metre because of the additional structural engineering, scaffolding, and weatherproofing required. You're looking at $4,000 to $6,000 per square metre for a second storey. Add in the cost of temporary accommodation if you can't live on site during the build, and the total for a 60-square-metre upper level can range from $240,000 to $360,000. It's a significant investment but often cheaper than moving to a bigger home in the same neighbourhood.

Council costs also play a role in Glen Waverley. Monash Council has specific planning overlays, especially in heritage or vegetation-protected areas. You'll need a planning permit for most external changes, which can add $3,000 to $8,000 in fees and consultant reports. A good builder will include these in your fixed-price quote from the start — never start an extension without a clear understanding of what permits are needed.

Melbourne's clay soils are another factor that can hit your budget. The eastern suburbs have reactive clay that expands and contracts with moisture. This means deeper footings and possibly piering, which adds $10,000 to $25,000 to the cost depending on the site. A soil test before you design can save you major surprises later. We always recommend budgeting an extra 10-15% for site-specific conditions.

The cheapest way to extend isn't always the cheapest in the long run. Going with a licensed builder who offers a fixed-price contract and a structural warranty might cost more upfront, but it protects you from cost blowouts and shoddy work. In Glen Waverley, where homes are long-term investments, quality pays back. If you want a ballpark for your specific property, call us for a free on-site consultation — we'll give you a real number, not a guess.

blogPosts.title: Knockdown Rebuild vs Renovation: Which is Better for Your Glen Waverley Block?
blogPosts.excerpt: Should you knock down and rebuild or renovate your Glen Waverley home? We compare costs, timelines, and outcomes for local homeowners.
body: Many homeowners in Glen Waverley face a tough choice: do you renovate your existing home or knock it down and start fresh? Both options have their pros and cons, and the right answer depends on your block, your budget, and your long-term plans. In this guide, we'll walk through the key differences to help you make an informed decision for your Glen Waverley property.

Renovating is usually the cheaper option upfront if you're happy with your current floor plan. A full home renovation in Glen Waverley typically costs between $150,000 and $400,000, depending on whether you're updating a few rooms or gutting the whole house. The main advantage is that you stay on your block — no moving costs, no disruption to your community. The downside is that you're limited by the existing structure: you can't easily change room layouts or add that extra bedroom without an extension.

A knockdown rebuild gives you a blank canvas. You can design a modern home that suits your lifestyle exactly, with open-plan living, energy-efficient materials, and the latest building standards. The cost in Glen Waverley starts around $350,000 for a basic three-bedroom home and can go well over $800,000 for a architect-designed residence. But you get a brand new home with a full warranty, and you're not patching up old plumbing or wiring.

Timelines differ significantly. A renovation can take 3 to 6 months for a major project. A knockdown rebuild from demolition to handover is usually 9 to 14 months. That extra time can be frustrating if you're living in temporary accommodation, but the result is a home that will last for decades with minimal maintenance. Many families in Glen Waverley choose the knockdown rebuild route because they love their location and don't want to move out of the school zone.

There's also the question of value. In Glen Waverley, a well-designed new home can be worth significantly more than a renovated old one. Real estate data shows that brand new builds in the area often sell for 20-30% more per square metre than renovated homes. So if you're planning to sell in the next 5-10 years, a knockdown rebuild might give you a better return on investment. But if you're staying put, the lower cost and shorter timeline of a renovation can be more appealing.

Ultimately, the best choice depends on your block size, the condition of your current home, and your budget. A narrow block might be better suited to a renovation, while a generous 800-square-metre lot could be perfect for a knockdown rebuild. At Skilled Builders Australia, we help Glen Waverley homeowners run the numbers on both options. Come to us for a free consultation — we'll walk your site and give you honest advice either way.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Building a New Home in Melbourne's Eastern Suburbs
blogPosts.excerpt: Building a new home in Melbourne's east? From selecting the right block to council approvals, this step-by-step guide covers everything.
body: Building a new home in Melbourne's eastern suburbs — from Glen Waverley to Box Hill, Mount Waverley to Camberwell — is an exciting journey, but it can feel overwhelming if you don't know the steps. In this guide, we'll take you through the entire process from start to finish, highlighting the specific considerations for building in Melbourne's east. Whether you're a first-time builder or knockdown-rebuilding, this is your blueprint.

Step one: choose your block wisely. In the eastern suburbs, many blocks come with established gardens, mature trees, and sometimes heritage overlays. Before you buy, check the council's planning scheme for any vegetation protection orders or overlay restrictions. Also, get a soil test — reactive clay is common in areas like Glen Waverley and Mount Waverley, which affects foundation costs. A good block with the right orientation can save you tens of thousands in the long run.

Step two: design and permits. You'll need a building permit and, for most blocks, a planning permit. In Monash and Whitehorse councils, planning permits can take 2 to 4 months, sometimes longer if neighbours object. Your builder should handle the submission and any negotiations with council. At Skilled Builders Australia, we've built strong relationships with local council planners, which helps the process run more smoothly. Expect to spend 4-8 weeks on design and a further 8-12 weeks on permits.

Step three: fixed-price contract and finance. Once permits are approved, your builder will issue a fixed-price contract with an itemised cost breakdown. This is your protection — never proceed with a builder who can't give you a locked-in price. You'll also need to secure financing. Most lenders in Melbourne will lend based on the fixed-price contract plus a 10% contingency. We recommend using a mortgage broker who specialises in construction loans, as the drawdown process is different from a standard home loan.

Step four: construction. Building a new home in the east typically takes 8 to 14 months from slab to handover, depending on size and complexity. You'll want a builder who provides regular updates — we send daily site photos and weekly progress reports. The key milestones are slab down, framing, lock-up, and fit-out. Melbourne's weather can cause delays, especially during winter, so a good builder builds weather contingencies into the schedule.

Step five: handover and warranty. After the final inspection and any defect fixes, you'll get the keys. Your new home should come with a 7-year structural warranty — this is mandatory in Victoria. Also ensure you have manuals for appliances, warranty documents, and a maintenance schedule. With the right builder, building a new home in Melbourne's eastern suburbs is a rewarding experience. Start with a free consultation — we'd love to show you what's possible on your block.

blogPosts.title: What to Expect When Building in Glen Waverley: Council, Soil, and Timing
blogPosts.excerpt: Building in Glen Waverley comes with its own rules. Learn about council requirements, soil conditions, and realistic timelines for your project.
body: Glen Waverley is one of Melbourne's most sought-after suburbs, and building here comes with specific challenges and opportunities. Whether you're planning a new home, extension, or knockdown rebuild, understanding the local conditions can save you time, money, and stress. In this guide, we'll cover the three biggest factors that affect building in Glen Waverley: council regulations, soil types, and how long things actually take.

Monash Council has a detailed planning scheme that protects the character of established neighbourhoods. If your property is in a Neighbourhood Character Overlay, you'll need to demonstrate that your new build or extension fits the surrounding streetscape. This often means limits on building height, setbacks, and materials. The council also protects significant trees — any tree with a trunk diameter over 30cm may require a report from an arborist. Factor 3-4 months for planning permits if your project is complex.

Soil conditions in Glen Waverley are dominated by reactive clay — specifically the basaltic and sedimentary clays that expand when wet and shrink when dry. This means your footings need to be deep enough to reach stable ground, typically 800mm to 1.5m, depending on the site classification. A class M or H site is common, requiring stiffened raft slabs or pier-and-beam systems. A soil test before design is non-negotiable. We include this in our initial consultation so you know the real cost from day one.

Timelines vary, but here's a realistic breakdown for a typical new home or extension in Glen Waverley. Concept and design: 4-6 weeks. Permit approvals: 8-16 weeks (including council and building surveyor). Construction: 8-14 months for a new home, 4-8 months for an extension. Add 2-4 weeks if there are delays with materials or weather. The key to staying on schedule is having a builder who orders materials early and communicates proactively. We give clients a weekly schedule update every Monday.

One thing many homeowners don't expect is the temporary accommodation situation. If you're renovating or extending while living on site, you'll need to plan for noise, dust, and loss of amenities like kitchen or bathroom for weeks at a time. Many Glen Waverley families choose to rent nearby for 2-4 months during the messy stage. Budget $15,000 to $30,000 for rent and storage if you need to move out temporarily. It's worth it for a stress-free build.

Finally, choose a builder who knows Glen Waverley inside out. A builder with local experience understands which council planners are strict, which soil engineers are reliable, and which suppliers deliver on time. At Skilled Builders Australia, we've been building in this suburb for over 12 years. We can give you a realistic timeline upfront and stick to it. If you're thinking about building in Glen Waverley, give us a call — we'll walk your site and tell you exactly what to expect.
